- `run(input)` returns untrusted user input EXACTLY as given, except ONE trailing newline, if present, is removed.
- Input is never interpreted: shell metacharacters, leading dashes, backslash sequences are all data.

```elixir
def run(input) do
  String.replace_suffix(input, "\n", "")
end
```

Alternatively `String.trim_trailing(input, "\n")` trims ALL trailing newlines — that would violate "ONE trailing newline". So use `String.replace_suffix`.
